observation.visible_scene: A close-up, eye-level view of several split and charred firewood logs arranged in the foreground against a heavily blurred green outdoor background (grass and foliage). A wedge-shaped split log sits on the left, a flat-topped log in the center, and a blackened log with a curled piece of bark on its tip on the right. Orange flames lick the edges of the logs and out-of-focus flame shapes glow in the upper-left/center background; thin white smoke wisps rise above the wood. The logs themselves remain in fixed positions throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: Flames on the right edge of the left log and at its base flicker, change shape, and vary in height continuously frame to frame, without the logs moving.

The blurred background flames in the upper-left/center grow and shrink in intensity and shift shape (e.g., a tall orange flame appears around t=0.2–0.5s and again around t=0.9–2.1s), consistent with ongoing combustion rather than a new ignition.

White smoke wisps drift upward and tend to accumulate and become more visible on the right side of the frame, especially near the charred right log, growing denser toward the end of the clip (t≈1.5–2.6s).
A flame at the bottom-left base of the left log brightens and enlarges in the latter part of the excerpt (t≈2.2–2.6s).
The positions of the three logs and the curled bark tip on the right log do not change; only the fire and smoke alter.
No camera pan, tilt, or zoom is evident; the framing of the logs stays constant, so observed motion is from the flames and smoke, not the viewpoint.
outside_clip_unknowns: What ignited the wood and the full extent of the fire beyond the cropped frame.
Whether the blurred background flames belong to the same fire or a separate one.
The outcome of the burning after the clip ends.
Whether the excerpt begins or ends at a meaningful event boundary (it does not; motion is already underway at t=0 and continues at t=2.667s).
uncertain_details: The background orange shapes are out of focus; whether they are flames, glowing embers, or light reflections cannot be confirmed.
Any very slight camera shake is indistinguishable from the flicker of the fire given the static background evidence.
The exact source point of the right-side smoke (the charred log vs. unseen material behind it) is not fully resolvable.

may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
